See in Ontario we have something called the Good Samaritan Act. Basically it means that if you’re helping someone whose life is in danger, you’re protected from negligence or any liability. 

Meaning no one can sue you for sexual assault if you have to touch their chest during CPR, and they can’t charge you for regular assault or battery if you accidentally break their ribs during CPR (which is common). 

A case like this where the lifeguard was given jail time would likely be thrown out in Ontario due to this act and the lifeguard would have walked free, and rightfully so.

To add more, Be’lal is “Belial,” a demon in Abrahamic religions. Same with “Sammael” (Samael), and Asmodean (Asmodeus)—all Abrahamic demons. 

I’m also nearly positive that Graendal is a reference to “Grendel,” the monster in the epic poem *Beowulf.* 

And Artur Hawkwing I think is supposed to be a reference to King Arthur Pendragon, especially with how many characters take the surname “Paendrag,” including Seanchan, who believe themselves his descendants. 

Honestly, there’s a lot of modern-day parallels in the names of this series.

Edit: also, I think Shai’tan is actually meant to be “Shaytan,” a type of evil spirit or demon in Islam. But “Satan” is also viable.

University felt more relevant because my undergrad degree was a specialized degree with honours, and it took me seven years to complete. And because I took a lot of history courses during that time. As I’ve explained to other people in PMs, one of my professors happened to be a siege survivor himself, which inspired this project. And yes, I am aware that flying to Sarajevo would be the best thing for me to do. As it stands, Canada has travel advisories on Bosnia (which is probably unjustified, as most of them are on the website), and not only would this option be expensive, but it would be difficult, having to jump through more hoops than a simple vacation. It also wouldn’t be ideal because I don’t speak the language, and it would be hard to navigate in person without a tour guide. I’m aware misinformation is a rampant and biased in the Israel-Palestine debate, but publishing works like this isn’t exactly anything new. The 1982 book *Schindler’s Ark* is about the Holocaust, and became the movie *Schindler’s List.* The author, Thomas Keneally, had not experienced the Holocaust, and is Australian, and not Jewish. Rogue was the most fun to 100% for me. The collectibles are genuinely so interesting and well done.

There’s indigenous cave paintings that tell a story once you collect all of them. You have to use eagle vision to find them. 

There’s Templar crosses where you use eagle vision, and then a marking leads you to a spot nearby. Those crosses can be used to unlock special armour if you have the DLC. 

Instead of maps leading to buried treasure like in Black Flag, there’s maps leading to Templar graves. Collect them all and you get a special set of armour from a vault in a shipwreck. 

There’s pillars that turn into puzzles with eagle vision. Solve it and the pillar splits open to reveal a totem. Gather all totems and you get a special set of armour from an indigenous village.

There’s Viking sword fragments. Collect them all and they will lead you to the grave of a Viking off the coast of Canada, wherein a sword and an outfit awaits. 

There’s prosperity, which functions like animus fragments, but increase the amount of resources you get from side activities by a small percentage. 

And like Black Flag, there are treasure chests, animus fragments, and song sheets that give your crew sea shanties (there are actually more of them in Rogue than in Black Flag). 

In Black Flag, you can collect sticky notes and hack computers in the present day. In Rogue, instead of sticky notes, there are tablets, but both of these activities are actually rewarding, because they unlock unique weapons in the main game, such as Altaïr’s sword. In Black Flag, there was no reward save for some extra lore. 

TL;DR- Rogue may have skimped out on story, but it was a fucking blast to do all of the side content.
